correctness.rationale: For a difference of probability measures the variation norm is twice the positive mass, here the sum of the three target deficits even when some approximating atoms go off fiber. A map from the connected base has a single target component. In the mixed case the identity component contributes at least |w-1/3|, which absorbs the scaling mismatch when taking 2/3 times the norm error of the normalized double-cover approximant. Its error is at least 2/n for n maps: the heaviest normalized coefficient is at least 1/n and its map must leave the fiber somewhere. This lower bound is attained by balanced equal atoms on the double cover via single-atom exchanges. Consequently reserving a 1/3 identity section and using n=m-1 double-cover maps gives 4/[3(m-1)]. If all mass goes to the identity sheet the error is at least 4/3; if all goes to the double cover the missed identity point costs 2/3, and at m<=2 a nonsection miss also leaves a double-cover fiber point empty. For one map the identity section attains 4/3. For equal weights a nonsection miss leaves at most m-1 on-fiber atoms, and discrete balancing gives half-errors 1/m, 1/m and 4/(3m) at residues 0,1 and 2. The proposed identity counts k,k,k+1 give stationary double-cover counts respectively (k-1,k),(k,k),(k,k) during exchanges. For even double allocation, swap two labels by successive opposite moves from a balanced configuration; for odd allocation, alternate majority-to-minority moves, allowing either a swap by two moves or reversal of which site has the larger count. Thus arbitrary required label configurations at edge endpoints can be joined. Trivialize over each closed edge interval, keep stationary labels on their lifts, and realize each moving label on a disjoint subinterval by a path in connected Y_2 between the prescribed lifted endpoints; this also works on loop edges. Matching vertex assignments give continuous global maps. Off-fiber movement cannot increase the deficit beyond that of stationary atoms alone. This independently checks the inputs of the cited transport lemmas and proves attainment; the repairs change attribution, not the theorem.
residual_risks: The bounded integer check does not test the graph gluing or replace the all-budget proof. The theorem depends on constant mixing coefficients, the one-plus-two connected-component structure and the supremum norm on real continuous functions.

evidence: The connected-cover formulas require connected total space; the zero-error remark requires sections exhausting the whole fiber. The present single section does not exhaust it.

Kim's sequential uniform and Hilbert–Schmidt/L2 results and Brown's qualitative measure-space results do not give fixed-budget C-space errors. Kim 1968 Theorem 2.4 requires a doubly stochastic measure absolutely continuous relative to product Lebesgue measure, unlike this fiber-supported kernel.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The larger classical theories either impose incompatible hypotheses or address topology/closure rather than a matching positive finite-budget error.

value.rationale: The smallest graph cover combining a global section and genuine monodromy gives two different sharp finite-budget laws, with attainment and unequal asymptotic penalties along congruence classes. Extending from the known two and three terms to every larger budget changes the kind of result: it quantifies the loss from equal weights and shows that one section never makes exact finite representation possible.
residual_risks: The exact progression and ratios do not classify other disconnected monodromies or nonuniform target masses.
